plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Exit high-beta names (METU, MUU, PLTU) that are below their stops.

Reduce SPY to 20% to further de-risk and reduce broad index exposure.
This plan aims for capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to small positions, reducing overall leverage.
Reduce high-beta names (METU, MUU, PLTU) to manage concentration and risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration.
Buy TZA for 4% to add some inverse exposure, balancing risk.
This plan aims for risk-first growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing some inverse exposure. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, MUU, PLTU) to lean into growth.
Trim SPY to 15% to free up capital for higher-conviction plays.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leveraged and high-beta exposure, which amplifies both upside and drawdown potential. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can incur substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged holdings (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces high-beta and leveraged exposure, favoring income-generating ETFs. While aiming for reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable.
